The 'energy' of x is defined on the same page as ||x||^2, so 'cannot exceed the total energy' equals 'at most the squared length'. Supports 'at most its length squared'. Stored quote is clipped mid-sentence - see minor finding.

Parseval's identity'), which is exactly what the source states. My previous finding - that this page was cited for a biconditional it does not state - is resolved: the story now cites only the forward implication here and proves the converse itself (see f18).

Supported on context: 'An orthonormal basis is an orthonormal system with the additional property that the linear span of S is dense in H', and the following sentences tie this to complete vs incomplete systems. Supports 'complete is strictly stronger than orthonormal'. See minor finding on truncation.

HTTP 200. Verbatim. The same page states the identity with an explicit universal quantifier ('for every x in H'), consistent with the story's formula card now carrying 'for all f'. Supports the Pythagoras analogue in an orthonormal basis.

HTTP 200. NEW FACT. Verbatim. This is the cited input for the mechanism's proved converse. The page's preceding sentence makes it exact: 'Completeness of an orthonormal system ... can be equivalently restated as: for every v in H, if <v,e_k> = 0 for all k, then v = 0.' The contrapositive - a nonzero v orthogonal to the whole system means the system is not complete - is precisely what the mechanism uses. Correctly sourced.

HTTP 200. Verbatim, but the stored quote is only the four-word tail 'also forms an orthonormal basis for'. Supported by the immediately preceding sentence, which spells out the set {1/sqrt2, cos x/sqrt2, sin x/sqrt2, ...} and states it 'also forms an orthonormal basis for L^2([-pi,pi])' - i.e. the constant-plus-cosines-plus-sines system the claim describes. The page normalises everything by 1/sqrt2 (period-normalised inner product); the mechanism uses 1/sqrt(2pi) and 1/sqrt(pi) for the plain integral inner product it defined, which I verified symbolically give exact equality, so this is a convention difference, not an error. See minor finding on the truncated quote.

HTTP 200. Verbatim. Directly supports 'density of the trigonometric basis's span follows from Stone-Weierstrass'. The mechanism's added parenthetical - that Stone-Weierstrass strictly gives uniform density of trigonometric polynomials among continuous periodic functions, with L^2 density by further steps - is correct standard mathematics and a more careful statement than the source, not an overreach beyond it; it does not attribute the refinement to the page.

HTTP 200. Verbatim, in 'Convergence theorems'. The clause 'completeness of the Fourier basis' directly supports 'The Fourier basis is complete'. The consequent ('so Parseval holds for every square-integrable f') is a valid inference the story draws from f15 (complete implies Parseval) and f19 (it is an orthonormal basis); the page's convergence result (s_N converges to s in L^2) is equivalent to Parseval. Completeness stated here as a premise for a convergence result rather than as a standalone theorem, but the assertion the claim needs is present.

HTTP 200. NEW FACT. Verbatim. Supports the mechanism's standing hypothesis 'Work in L^2(-pi, pi), the square-integrable functions'; the page lists spaces of square-integrable functions as examples of Hilbert spaces.

findings.detail: Three stored quotes are clipped mid-sentence, each stopping immediately before the noun that carries the claim, because the source sentence continues into inline math that the extractor drops. f14 ends at 'the total energy of' (omitting 'x'); f16 ends at 'the linear span of' (omitting 'S is dense in H'); f19 ends at 'also forms an orthonormal basis for' (omitting 'L^2([-pi,pi])'). All three are genuinely verbatim substrings of their pages and all three are supported once the surrounding sentence is read, so none fails on quote_found or supports_claim. But a quote that ends before its load-bearing noun is weak as standalone evidence: a later reader or automated re-check working from the stored string alone could not confirm the claim without re-opening the page. Recommend extending each quote to the end of its clause. This does not affect the verdict.
findings.evidence: Full page sentences: '...the sum of these contributions cannot exceed the total energy of x.'; 'An orthonormal basis is an orthonormal system with the additional property that the linear span of S is dense in H.'; '...also forms an orthonormal basis for L^2([-pi,pi]).' The stored quotes stop at 'of', 'span of', and 'basis for' respectively.
